source.title: Farkas layers: don't shift the data, fix the geometry
source.authors: Aram-Alexandre Pooladian; Chris Finlay; Adam M. Oberman

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation affecting the reported experiments.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports CIFAR and ImageNet classification experiments comparing Farkas layers with standard residual networks, including training curves and training failures. These results bear on whether the tested networks train successfully under different normalization, initialization, and learning-rate conditions, using classification error and accuracy rather than the versions’ exact protocols.
record.gate_note: Rows capture reported test-error comparisons and explicit training outcomes. The paper reports test misclassification rates, not training classification error values in the tables; training curves are figures without tabulated values, so no exact training-error rows are extracted from them. Discussion of prior studies is not treated as this paper’s results.
record.test_reason: The study directly qualifies the Fixup component of V6: without input data normalization, Fixup still converges faster but requires a smaller learning rate. Its successful Fixup training also bears on the normalization-free residual-training component of V3. It does not test plain-network depth degradation, activation-matched initialization, or near-zero training error.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors propose Farkas layers as an architectural alternative that enables larger-rate training without BN and with default initialization, and report an early ImageNet advantage when combined with BN. Qualify this by recipe: the best-practice FarkasNet34 also uses zero initialization of the last layer in each block. The construction guarantees at least one active neuron per layer, not that every neuron remains active.
record.recipe_differences: Farkas layers add a linearly dependent row to layer weights to guarantee at least one active neuron; residual-network image-classification experiments compare this construction with standard ResNets and report test error and figure-based training curves.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch normalization, dataset, network depth, learning rate, Farkas aggregation choice (sum or mean), and input data normalization are varied or discussed as affecting outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Farkas layers improve final test error relative to standard residual networks, especially when BN is removed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding a constrained dependent component to residual layers can improve generalization performance under the tested training recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: With BN in both architectures, FarkasNets show an approximately 20% first-epoch improvement on ImageNet; the advantage diminishes later.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Farkas architecture modifications can improve early ImageNet performance even when BN is already present.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean-aggregation FarkasNet101 trains at LR 0.1 without BN, whereas the default-initialized standard alternative completely fails.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A Farkas architecture modification can enable large-learning-rate residual training without BN or specialized initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: One of three CIFAR-100 ResNet50 runs without BN made no progress in its first five epochs and was excluded from the reported average.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested standard residual recipe without BN can fail to start learning.

fits_no_version.finding: The best-practice FarkasNet34 recipe tolerates LR 0.05 and obtains 7.12% test error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mean aggregation and zero initialization of the last block layer permit improved FarkasNet training at an intermediate learning rate.

record.problems: Most reported table values are test misclassification, not training classification error. CIFAR values are averages across three runs and the paper gives no uncertainty estimates; failed runs are omitted from averages and marked with an asterisk. Training curves are figures without exact values stated in text. The ImageNet comparison is limited to 30 epochs.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. Figures 2–7 contain training curves but exact training-error values are not stated and should not be reconstructed from plots.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error is not established by the supplied text; test error and successful training do not establish it. Random/corrupted labels are not tested.
No two-layer teacher-student experiment, spurious-minimum frequency, or student-width intervention.
No plain-versus-residual comparison, plain BN-network depth degradation, longer-training control, or very deep plain tanh experiment.
No activation-matched initialization comparison in plain networks, signal/gradient propagation measurement, orthogonal-versus-Gaussian comparison, or extreme-depth convolution experiment.
No stability threshold, initial linearized model, curvature trajectory, catapult recovery, or edge-of-stability measurement.
The original sigmoid MNIST, VGG, and Inception settings are not replicated. Exact convergence-rate differences cannot be read from the supplied figure text.

missing.what: A qualitative training-outcome row for Fixup34: successful and faster convergence without BN, but only after reducing LR when inputs are not normalized. R37 currently records only final test error.
missing.locator: Section 4, Impact of Data Normalization and Best Practice Comparison; paragraph preceding Table 4

missing.what: Learning-rate capacity should be an explicit outcome for the BN, standard non-BN, and Fixup recipes, rather than only a condition attached to final test error.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Final test-error differences do not establish training-error, convergence-speed, or initialization claims. The supplied figure text lacks readable curve traces, so no numerical training endpoints or speed differences are inferred. Figure-only curves are already declared in rows_left_out; missing entries concern explicit prose and table outcomes.

versions.untested_parts: The paper studies CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 and reports training curves, but does not tabulate training classification error or test random/corrupted labels, Adam, or smaller models and early stopping.
The paper does not test two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems or student width relative to teacher width.

The reported experiments compare residual networks with and without batch normalization; they do not compare plain networks with identity-shortcut networks, or test the specific He et al. depth claim.

The paper uses default PyTorch initialization and tests a Farkas-layer modification; it does not compare activation-matched initialization schemes, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, or 10,000-layer plain networks.
The paper does not study learning-rate stability thresholds, curvature, sharpness, or loss recovery above a stability limit.

It compares batch-normalized and non-batch-normalized networks on CIFAR and compares Farkas layers with batch normalization on ImageNet; it does not test the cited sigmoid MNIST or VGG/Inception settings, nor Fixup.
